audit_notes: Model: steady 1D energy balance in a porous spine pile (x=0 wall surface, x=1 pile tips, z = x*L): k_eff*T''/L^2 = H_v*(T - T_a) - S(x), with Beer-Lambert absorption of the non-reflected sun S = (1-rho)*kappa*I*exp(-kappa*L*(1-x)). Wall boundary: conduction from the pile plus transmitted sun absorbed by the painted wall minus the wall's sky loss through the gap fraction exp(-kappa*L) equals the wall conduction U*(T(0)-T_in). Tip boundary: film exchange and part of the sky loss. Checks: kappa*L = 2.4 (9 % gap fraction) for 2 mm rods at ~8 mm spacing is consistent; H_v = 500 W/m3K = h_rod (~20 W/m2K at 1-2 m/s) x specific surface (~25 m2/m3); k_eff = 0.2 W/mK. Fin parameter sqrt(H_v*L^2/k_eff) = sqrt(500*0.0016/0.2) = 2.0, i.e. the pile dumps most absorbed heat to the air before it reaches the wall. Baseline: bare painted wall = no rods (kappa = 0) with air exchange raised to H_v = 1125 so that the wall-to-air coupling sqrt(k_eff*H_v) = 15 W/m2K equals the normal outer film coefficient; this reproduces the direct sol-air result for the painted wall (5.56 vs 5.59 W/m2). My own numerical solution: daily mean (I=180, T_a=35 C) q = 5.19 vs 5.56 W/m2 (-7 %); peak hour (I=700, T_a=43 C) wall surface 47.0 C vs 54.9 C and q = 11.0 vs 15.0 W/m2 (-27 %). So the pile mainly cuts the peak load; the daily-mean gain against an already white wall is small because the pile also blocks the wall's sky loss. Structural: glass-ceramic rods 2 mm x 40 mm cantilevers carry wind drag easily but are brittle against impact; stainless wire alternative. Maintenance: dust, leaves and nesting birds (the pile resembles anti-bird spikes, which deters birds). Simulation coefficient: fin parameter 2.0.
